paper.title: Spread of epidemic disease on networks

headline: Newman 2002 SIR-on-networks (bond percolation): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; T_c(hom)=0.251 (formula) vs emp-onset 0.223; heterogeneity collapses T_c to 0.038 (SF); GF final-size tracks simulation within 0.001 at T in {0.3,0.4,0.6}

verdicts.gate: P1 homogeneous epidemic threshold matches T_c = <k>/(<k^2>-<k>) from the realized degree sequence
P2 degree heterogeneity lowers the threshold: T_c(power-law) < 0.5*T_c(homogeneous) and < 0.10
P3 generating-function final size S=1-g0(1-T+Tu), u=g1(...) matches simulation at T in {0.3,0.4,0.6}; no outbreak below T_c

extra.framing: network-generation + bond-percolation (SIR isomorphism), NOT autonomous agent-stepping
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published network-epidemiology result; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce Newman's percolation threshold, its heterogeneity-driven collapse, and the generating-function final size, and would catch an artifact

citations: Newman, M.E.J. (2002). Spread of epidemic disease on networks. Physical Review E 66:016128. doi:10.1103/PhysRevE.66.016128.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the closed-form threshold + generating-function final-size curve
